problem_statement: MatthewGreenberg/shoe-finder ("Perfect Pair") is a WebGL sneaker-discovery storefront built with Next.js 16 (Pages Router), React-Three-Fiber and framer-motion. A full-screen three.js scene renders a scrollable/zoomable wall of 144 shoe tiles from a local catalogue, with a fixed "PERFECT PAIR" masthead and a floating glass "control island" at the bottom that switches collection (Nike / New Balance / Under $150), filters Nike by model (All / Jordan / Dunk) and zooms. Because the wall is a WebGL canvas, the shopper never sees a legible list of what actually matched their filter or how many pairs there are. Extend the finder with a docked "MATCHES" results shelf (src/components/FinderShelf.jsx): a DOM panel that lists the shoes matching the CURRENT finder state as product cards (thumbnail, title, price) under a live count header ("N matches · <collection> <filter>"), reading the app's own catalogue and matchesFilter predicate. The shelf must (1) follow every browse context — it renders for the Nike, New Balance AND Under $150 collections — (2) re-render its cards + count header live whenever the model filter or collection changes, and (3) lay out its result cards responsively so the 390px mobile view has no horizontal overflow, while keeping the PERFECT PAIR masthead, the WebGL wall, the control island (collection tabs, All/Jordan/Dunk filters, zoom) and the minimap exactly as they are. The per-viewport card-row layout lives in src/components/finderShelfLayout.js and the shelf styling in src/styles/globals.css.
required_content: A docked "MATCHES" finder results shelf (.finder-shelf) is present, listing the shoes that match the current finder state as product cards (each result card carries the class .finder-shelf__card, with thumbnail + title + price) under a live "N matches · <collection> <filter>" count header labelled with the class .finder-shelf__label.
The results shelf follows every browse context: it renders for the Nike, New Balance and Under $150 collections (not only the default Nike view).
Clicking a model filter chip (Jordan / Dunk) or switching collection re-renders the shelf's cards and updates its count header to reflect the active filter.
The 390px mobile home view has no horizontal overflow: the result cards wrap so the document does not scroll sideways.

The PERFECT PAIR masthead, the WebGL shoe wall, the control island (Nike / New Balance / Under $150 tabs, All / Jordan / Dunk filters, zoom) and the minimap remain present and functional; no new remote requests, console errors or uncaught exceptions are introduced.
design_constraints: The results shelf must read as part of the Perfect Pair storefront: the airy off-white glass panel, dark-on-light legible count header and card typography — not a detached dark chrome or an illegible low-contrast panel.
The shelf's result cards must lay out cleanly (wrap on mobile) without overlapping, shingling or clipping cards or colliding title/price text.

Keep the fix confined to the finder shelf component + its layout module + the shelf styling (src/components/FinderShelf.jsx, src/components/finderShelfLayout.js, src/styles/globals.css); do not restyle the 3D scene or the control island.
Do not remove, hide or truncate any control-island filter/collection/zoom control; the shelf must reflect the finder state, never replace the island.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the Perfect Pair wall at 1440px with the finder results shelf showing the Nike matches and the control island at the bottom; no horizontal overflow.
mobile_initial captures the same view at 390px; the result cards must wrap so there is no horizontal overflow.
tablet_initial captures the 834px view of the same layout.
desktop_dunk_filter captures the state after clicking the Dunk model filter; the shelf re-renders to the Dunk matches and the count header reads "... Nike Dunk".
desktop_new_balance captures the state after switching to the New Balance collection; the results shelf follows the collection (still present, count header "... New Balance All").
desktop_under_150 captures the state after switching to the Under $150 collection; the results shelf is still present.
mobile_under_150 captures the 390px Under $150 view; no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The finder results shelf is present and lists the matching shoes as product cards with a live count header.
Switching model filter or collection re-renders the shelf cards and updates the count header.
The PERFECT PAIR masthead and control-island interactions remain functional.
design_consistency: The shelf keeps the Perfect Pair glass panel + dark-on-light legible count header and card typography.
The WebGL wall, masthead and control island are visually unchanged aside from the added shelf.
regression: The production build serves via next start and the WebGL wall renders.
The masthead, results shelf and control island all remain reachable and interactive.
responsive: The 390px mobile initial and mobile filtered views have no horizontal overflow.
The result cards wrap or reflow cleanly on mobile rather than overlapping or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 16 + React-Three-Fiber extend_interaction task on the Perfect Pair shoe-finder wall. The native lever is the finder's own results surface: a docked MATCHES shelf that lists the shoes matching the current filter as product cards with a live count header, reading the app's existing catalogue + matchesFilter predicate. Four orthogonal discriminators: D6 no_horizontal_overflow on the mobile shelf card row, D3 visual_regression on the shelf palette/legibility + card layout, D2 dom_assertions on the shelf's cross-collection presence (New Balance + Under $150), and D4 interaction_assertions on the Dunk filter re-rendering the count header. Runtime is clean (local catalogue + local font stack; swiftshader WebGL warnings are benign, not console errors).

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Perfect Pair WebGL sneaker-discovery wall (Next.js 16 + React-Three-Fiber). extend_interaction: add the finder's own DOM results shelf over the WebGL wall and make it follow the collection, re-render on filter, and lay out responsively; discriminated by four orthogonal deterministic gates (D6 overflow, D3 visual, D2 cross-collection, D4 filter).
